implementation_notes: Default in-process realization: a module-level dict keyed by string with a @register decorator doing fail-fast duplicate detection at class-definition time and a lookup function raising LookupError for unknown keys. Registration happens as an import side effect, so the import graph is the wiring.
pitfalls: A module that is never imported registers nothing, so discovery is invisible in the source: plugins must be imported (or scanned with pkgutil.walk_packages/entry points) and import errors fail the whole start-up.
Module-level dicts live for the process and leak between tests; a fixture must clear or snapshot/restore the registry (or make the registry an instance).

The check-then-set in register is not atomic across threads even under the GIL (the interpreter may switch between the membership test and the assignment), so start-up registration should be single-threaded or locked.

variants.name: Packaging entry points (importlib.metadata)
variants.implementation_notes: Cross-distribution discovery: each provider package declares entry points in pyproject.toml under a group name, and the host resolves them with importlib.metadata.entry_points(group=...) and EntryPoint.load(). The installed distribution metadata is the registry, the group name is the key domain, and no host code lists plug-ins; report packages are visible without importing anything until load().
pitfalls: Discovery reads installed metadata only: running from a source checkout without an install (or with a stale metadata cache) finds nothing, and editable installs must be refreshed after metadata changes.
Entry-point names are loose strings in package metadata, so duplicates and typos surface at runtime; validate names and detect collisions in the host.
ep.load() executes third-party import code at discovery time - a broken or hostile provider raises during enumeration and must be caught per entry point.
